newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Katoen Natie invests 250 mln Bfr at Opel Belgium.
newsitem.headline: Katoen Natie invests 250 mln Bfr at Opel Belgium.

text.p: Katoen Natie, a leading cargo-handling and stevedoring company in the Belgian port of Antwerp, said on Tuesday it would invest 250 million francs to expand its supply centre at General Motors' (GM) Opel Belgium assembly unit.
"Katoen Natie will soon start the expansion works for the second stage of its Supply In Line Sequence (SILS) centre at Opel Belgium," it said in a statement.
The storage capacity will be more than doubled to 17,250 from 8,500 square metres.

Katoen Natie said it would construct a copy of the existing warehouse, adjacent to the existing SILS centre which had been used since August 1995 to store bumpers for the Astra and Vectra models, and cooling modules for the Vectras.
From 1998, it will also store cooling modules for the Astras, it said.

"The SILS concept fits in the strategic option of Opel Belgium to invite suppliers to settle as close as possible to our plant," Opel Belgium president and managing director Leo Valvekens said in the statement.
"For Opel Belgium the main goal is to strenghten its competitive position by reducing logistic costs per produced car," he said.
